invariants: A count pairs objects with number words one to one, and its last word names the whole group — which is why order, spacing, and arrangement can change without changing the answer for kch one more group.
misconceptions: Skipping or double-counting an object, recounting when nothing changed, or believing a spread-out group holds more.

widget.prompt: There are 8 stars and 3 hearts. Which statement is true?

options.label: More stars
options.feedback: Correct — 8 stars against 3 hearts; matching them one to one leaves stars unmatched.

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: The groups are equal only when both counts match; here the counts are 8 and 3.

options.label: More hearts
options.feedback: Pairing them up one to one uses every heart; the hearts do not outnumber the stars here.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can always tell — pair the groups one to one and see which side has leftovers.

commonLandings.feedback: 7 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 8.
9 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 7 lands on 8.

widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 7 means one hop, stopping on 8.
